reason: The cited evidence shows that high-entropy effects and porosity can lower thermal conductivity (E1, E4) and that mass/strain fluctuations scatter phonons (E2), but none of the passages demonstrate or validate a predictive model that integrates these descriptors to achieve the claimed quantitative improvements. The specific premises about model accuracy and error reduction are unsupported by the cited studies.
premises: High-entropy descriptors (size/mass mismatch, configurational entropy) and microstructural features (dual-porosity) are key to predicting low phonon thermal conductivity.
Severe lattice distortions and controlled porosity enhance phonon scattering and reduce mean free path.
Conventional averaged-property approaches poorly capture disorder parameters and microstructural features.
Integrating these descriptors will reduce prediction error by 20–30% vs. conventional methods.
The model will predict lattice thermal conductivity within ~10% of experimental measurements.
